messages.subject: Scores vs Factors
parts:
Hello Phil and everybody else.
First of all, congratulations on the package and on this forum.

This is a basic (and possibly theoric) question, probably related to the meaning of each column on summary. I'm sorry to bother you but I am really stuck.

I am using a GRADED model with 2 dimensions (specified by using model=2). 
When I call summary() and use the parameter NONE for rotation I get the expected zero correlation between factors. But when I use fscores to create the scores, I get some correlation between the scores. 

The question: Shouldn't the scores also have zero correlation?

This is the code:
mirt_infra_2 = mirt(Diretor_infra, 1, itemtype = "graded", model=2,
                   technical=list(removeEmptyRows=TRUE, NCYCLES = 100000, MAXQUAD=40000, 
                                  BURNIN=300, SEMCYCLES=200) )
scores_infra_2 = fscores(mirt_infra_2, rotate='none', verbose=T)

summary(mirt_infra_2, verbose=T, rotate='none')
cor(scores_infra_2)

On Thu, Mar 22, 2018 at 10:25 AM, Roberto Maranhão <rmar...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello Phil and everybody else.
First of all, congratulations on the package and on this forum.

This is a basic (and possibly theoric) question, probably related to the meaning of each column on summary. I'm sorry to bother you but I am really stuck.

I am using a GRADED model with 2 dimensions (specified by using model=2). 
When I call summary() and use the parameter NONE for rotation I get the expected zero correlation between factors. But when I use fscores to create the scores, I get some correlation between the scores. 

The question: Shouldn't the scores also have zero correlation?

No. Rotation != correlation when in reference to the factor scores, even when modelled this way explicitly via confirmatory models. This is actually the point of factor rotations, to uncover the likely relationships between the latent factors by simply re-expressing the factor loadings as a new, and usually more simplified, basis. The rotation in fscores() will likely give more meaning to the saved scores, analogous to what summary() does, but does not constrain all the properties (such as orthogonality) when computed. HTH.

Phil
